correctness.rationale: The normalized mean-zero operator is Q_n S Q_n on each strict-input-order chamber. Every selector column is chosen at most three times, yielding the analytic sqrt(3) upper bound. For n=4,5, CHECK.py exhausts all 24/120 strict orders (12/60 distinct selectors) and checks positive semidefiniteness of 2 n^2 C - C S^T C S C (C=nI-11^T) by exact rational Schur complements, equivalent to the squared centered norm bound 2. Exact local selectors at (1,0,2,3) and (0,3,4,1,2) attain squared ratio 2. For all n>=6, a six-site core and explicit added coordinates force columns 1 and 4 to be selected three times each, and perturbation e_1-e_4 attains squared ratio 3; n=2 is a swap and n=3 a spatial constant. Ties are covered by continuity, and local-to-global control follows from finite-piece affine continuity. Finite all-small-order enumeration is exhaustive, while large-n diagnostic tests are not substituted for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest published arithmetic-saturation claim concerns ordinary uncentered l_p perturbation norms. At n=5 its uncentered l_2 ceiling sqrt(3) is achievable by a singly tripled selection column, whereas the mean-centered quotient norm proved here equals sqrt(2), so the exact centered claim is neither the same statement nor an unmodified special case. The published three-point BV threshold concerns adjacent-edge differences, not the centered Euclidean seminorm. Maragos–Schafer establish filter representations, Little–Jones prove one-input total-variation decrease, neither implying this two-input centered classification. Full text for the two close public finding records was inaccessible; this is a material priority risk but their summaries do not decisively cover the new five-site centering distinction.

value.rationale: The exact centered-Hilbert norm is the canonical perturbation measure after removing an irrelevant common baseline from cyclic median smoothing. The result is a complete all-size classification of a natural nonlinear operator invariant, revealing that a single tripled-selection column can saturate raw l2 amplification at five sites but cannot saturate the translation-quotient Hilbert norm. Six sites are necessary and sufficient for two independent triply selected columns to balance input and output means and realize the full sqrt(3) ceiling. This distinguishes genuine two-input stability from the known one-input total-variation smoothing and supplies a nontrivial exact boundary useful for baseline-invariant noise sensitivity.
